note: Every pin is in Canada. Lives that ended here sit at the grave where the record gives one, otherwise at the place of death, offset slightly so neighbours in one city can be told apart. A few are pinned where they were born or, in Ann Maria Jackson's case, where she settled; the card says which.

people.name: Albert Jackson
people.blurb: Born into slavery in Delaware and carried north to Toronto by his mother on the Underground Railroad. In 1882 he became Toronto's first Black letter carrier, and kept the post only because his community refused to let prejudice take it from him. He died in Toronto in 1918 and is buried here, in the Necropolis.

people.name: Ann Maria Jackson
people.blurb: Albert Jackson's mother. After two of her eldest children were sold and her husband died in a poorhouse, she learned four more were about to be sold and fled in November 1858 with the seven still with her, by way of Wilmington, Philadelphia and St. Catharines to Toronto. Escaping with seven children was almost unheard of. She is pinned to the Ward, where the family settled; the record does not say where she died.
